chapter: Jamming, bootleg records and the Topsy hit
title: Why hit records are unpredictable
summary: Cole and Kirchner discuss editing, and Jonah Jones's 'Baubles, Bangles and Beads' hit.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: From my own experience with recording, you know, I just feel, especially if you have any kind of arrangement or anything, you have to do the editing yourself.
Because only you know how everything fits together.

And then I would say this. A lot of times, I know Jonah was telling me, he said, Cozy, when I picked one of his records, was "Baubles, Bangles and Beads," he said, Cozy on the record date, he said that was just thrown in on one of the last numbers. He said "what I spent a lot of time on and what we thought was going to be it was "Rose Room." He said we spent some time on that trying to get it together to sound good. And he said "Baubles, Bangles and Beads" was one of those things we just got a hit on the last moment.
And that was the one that took off, so you never know which one is going to be a hit, you know.
That's been true of a lot of things, I guess, Coleman Hawkins' 'Body and Soul' was like that. It's just done as a little after thought in the studio. Didn't even have a chart on it.
No, didn't have a chart on it. So that's the way those things go.
Well it must have been a nice surprise for you.
Oh yes, it was beautiful. I just didn't realize that it was making all that noise until it did. Until it really did.
